items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I dont remember who was in Lou Russell's band when they played at the Savoy on Easter Monday 1929 with us

ctx.x: But we preferred to remain as we were and after the first two shows, we found out that our experience in that kind of work was not very strong. We had to play a curtain call number which is a number that is played before the show begins and we could not get ourselves together sitting in a pit below the stage. We thought that if we played on the stage it would be better. The manager of the theater let us try it and we went over big. The public could see Cecil with his high hat dancing in front of the orchestra and…

After Christmas of 1928 and New Years 1929 we went on another tour and came back to the 'Track' on Easter Monday of 1929. Three orchestras played that Monday for 12 hours of dancing. Fess Williams, Lou Russell and Lloyd Scott.

Things went fine for us at the Savoy until Lloyd got drunk one night, had an argument with Buchanan and took a swing at him. But like Bull Williams, Lloyd missed because Buchanan knew that it was going to happen as it was not the first time someone had tried to knock his head off. He knew when to duck. One of the bouncers who was always near when Buchanan had words with someone,
